scope_choices: This is automated API model review, not independent human verification, replication or clinical validation.

The assigned PDF hash was recomputed and matches assignments.json. Image binaries were not directly reopened during this synthesis; all visual descriptions remain attributed to inherited page/image-review notes.
All ten page texts are supplied. Earlier page-review notes contain batch-local statements that other pages were unavailable; these do not mean the assembled ten-page text is incomplete.
The 80 previously uncovered operational features now have one disposition each; no executable JSON Schema validation, graph assembly, or KG admission was run.
No executable JSON Schema validation, cross-reference validator, graph assembly or KG admission was run in this response.
Primary transition semantics are acquisition angle around a static anatomy, not clinical elapsed time, disease progression, treatment response or physiological change.

The narrow L3 mapping is a reviewer interpretation of same-input, two-direction angular predictions in Figure 2, not an author-stated treatment counterfactual capability. Its visual basis is inherited from supplied image-review notes.
No optimizer, learned action-selection policy, closed-loop clinical control or L4 decision result is demonstrated by the described pipeline.
CT-derived synthetic projection holdouts support R1 synthesis feasibility, not R2 actual-human transition validation. R2 is separately scoped to CheXpert clinical-image classification.
The source does not sufficiently identify whether the NLST downstream frontal/lateral inputs are acquired radiographs or simulated projections.
Overlap between CT pretraining subjects and downstream NLST train/validation/test subjects is not reported; leakage is unresolved, not established.
CycleGAN fitting data, test-split independence, pathology preservation and adaptation ablations are not reported.
The 1,000 CT-volume corpus is described with a patient-level 70:10:20 split, but realized split counts, unique-patient count and exact synthesis analysis count are not reported.
CheXpert counts are CXRs rather than unique patients; patient-level split safeguards, demographics and per-pathology counts are not reported.
The CVD endpoint definition, prediction horizon, event counts, follow-up and censoring handling are not sufficiently specified.
Table 2's printed Xray2Xray mean 0.843 appears inconsistent with its displayed five pathology scores. All reported values are preserved without substitution.
The CVD numerical advantage over BI-Mamba has reported DeLong p=0.1326. A statistically significant advantage over every comparator is not established.
AUROC confidence intervals, training-seed variability, multiplicity handling and CheXpert significance tests are not reported.
Table 3's ± quantities are not defined as standard deviations, standard errors or intervals; their aggregation unit is not reported.
A categorical generative distribution and descriptive variability do not establish calibrated uncertainty, epistemic/aleatoric separation or joint trajectory coverage.
Table 3 averages across angular positions. Figure 2 is illustrative, not an aggregate drift-versus-horizon validation. No effective horizon at a declared tolerance is reported.
The 24-layer/12-layer comparison also changes parameter count. A controlled mechanism ablation proving that 3D context causes the downstream advantage is not reported.
Whether Transformer parameter counts include VQ-GAN components is not reported.
VQ-GAN reconstruction and unseen-view synthesis are different tasks; their PSNR/SSIM should not be treated as directly equivalent forecasting endpoints.
Filtered-back-projection examples do not establish patient-specific CT equivalence. Quantitative volumetric/HU accuracy, lesion preservation and diagnostic reconstruction fidelity are not reported.

The upper row of Figure 3 is labeled ground-truth reconstruction, not explicitly untouched original CT slices. Slice coordinates, voxel dimensions, windowing and the represented patient count are not reported.
The paper acknowledges reconstruction information loss and domain/generalizability limitations.
CheXpert classification after retraining and adaptation is not external validation of an unchanged NLST classifier, and the two datasets do not establish a validated multiscale composition.

Clinical effect identification, actual reader evaluation, prospective shadow/interventional use, realized clinical benefit and authorization with monitoring are not reported. Cited systems' capabilities are not inherited.

Security tests, memorization audits, privacy safeguards, ethics/IRB approval, governance applicability, operational monitoring, code/weight release and asset licenses are not reported in the supplied paper; public availability or compliance was not independently checked.
The complete supplied ontology criteria were used for the 80 additional feature dispositions; the output remains unvalidated by an executable schema validator.
